speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs. To help me determine the cause, could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they worsen after physical activity or improve with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia that worsens with looking up or down, and proximal muscle weakness that fatigues with activity but improves with rest, is the classic clinical presentation of this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
